Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
33 pages, 17 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers for the same number of loops during prefill and decode, despite asymmetric serving costs: on batch-1 chain-of-thought tasks, prefill takes under 3% of wall time while decoding takes over 97%. We ask whether prefill and decode should loop equally, and find they should not: untying the two loop counts reads the prompt with more loops and decodes with fewer. Across dense and 26.4B sparse-MoE backbones, a two-regime law emerges. On fixed-depth models or single-loop decoders, naive untying collapses; we introduce LoopBridge, a lightweight adapter (2.4% of parameters on Ouro-2.6B; 0.13-0.25% on 26.4B MoEs) with cache-foldable prompt KV maps and decoder LoRA that serves any trained pair at native decode speed. On Ouro-2.6B at one decode loop, four prefill loops lift the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 to 58.2 (vs. 49.5 for tied distillation); on Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, 4/2 stays within 0.8 points of 4/4 across eight benchmarks and matches its GSM8K accuracy at 2.0x throughput. At 26.4B sparse-MoE scale in vLLM across five reasoning and 256K-1M benchmarks, LoopBridge sweeps tied distillation 5/5 under controlled 24M budgets (+7.8 on 3/1; +5.1 on fixed-depth Inkling-2-Mini 3/2, rescuing a 2.2% training-free collapse). On variable-depth 26.4B MoEs at two or three decode loops (27,950 four-sample rollouts), training-free untying works natively, and 0.017-0.025%-parameter prompt KV-only maps (zero decode overhead) lift 4/2 by +2.6 points (+4.0 on 256K-1M tasks, +9.5 on 512K MRCR) over 2/2 at 1.75x decode speed vs. 4/4, while 4/3 recovers 99.8% of 4/4 (74.5 vs. 74.7) at 1.27x-1.29x speed. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge
